clue.text: Boy's ambition to go with Virgin ere end appears?

indicators.note: what appears out of the jumble is a new word formed from those letters, so the phrase is to be rearranged

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A boy dreams of a railway career with Virgin, the British train operator, before it all ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgin Trains ran British intercity services, which makes the train-driving reading of the surface feel natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving a railway locomotive was the classic childhood career dream of small boys in Britain.

clue.text: See 5 across
Awfully fine story, too good to put into words?

definitions.text: too good to put into words

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the word beside it comes out mangled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a fable is a short moral tale

explanation.surface: Someone praises a tale as so wonderful that no description could do it justice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineffable describes something so great or extreme that language cannot express it.

clue.text: The fossil that wasn't one broken outside the menagerie

indicators.note: a broken thing has its parts scattered, so the word's letters are reassembled differently
the jumbled word sits outside, wrapping round the other piece

blocks.note: the word one, rearranged
a menagerie is a collection of wild animals, a zoo

explanation.surface: A broken specimen kept beside an animal collection turns out not to be a real fossil after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Eozoon canadense was a Canadian rock structure hailed in the 1860s as the oldest fossil, later shown to be purely mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous banded rock was claimed as a primitive organism's remains but proved to be inorganic.

clue.text: So-and-so vicar's baptismal request?

blocks.note: first meaning: a person whose ... escapes you
second meaning: what a priest asks at a christening, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase used for someone you cannot name is also, taken word by word, the question a clergyman asks before baptising a baby boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a casual placeholder for a forgotten person and a literal question about a child's given name.

clue.text: Pooh's hums - even the cows can do them with increased forward pressure

indicators.note: to do something to words here is to work them over, so the preceding letters are reworked into a fresh order

blocks.note: every letter of these words, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh's little songs are so simple that even cattle could perform them.
explanation.walkthrough: A twenty-letter anagram; the definition is playful, since the idiom literally escalates from pushing to shoving.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at the critical moment, and literally a push upgraded to a shove is stronger forward force.

clue.text: Caveman partly on song, a sacred one

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, so its outer letters are trimmed away

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut down
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A prehistoric man bursts into song, and a holy one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the inner AVEM of the first word survives; 'on' means placed after, and 'one' in the definition refers back to song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hail Mary is a Catholic prayer famously set to music by Schubert and Gounod, a religious song.

clue.text: See 5
Warm places in the valley the Ordnance Survey has correctly included

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one piece is held within another
something included is taken in, placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a glen is a Scottish valley
the standard abbreviation for Britain's mapping agency
OK means all correct

explanation.surface: A map-maker accurately marks the sheltered spots in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey is Britain's national mapping agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Inglenooks are cosy seats built into the recess of a large open fireplace, hence snug heated spots.

clue.text: At the heart of remembered sleep, let's start to misappropriate

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the central letters of the next word are kept
the start of a word is its opening, so just its beginning is used

blocks.note: the central four letters of this ten-letter word
the cartoon sign for snoring
the opening two letters

explanation.surface: Someone at the centre of half-remembered dreams sets out to steal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' here takes two letters, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: To embezzle is to steal money one has been entrusted with, a form of misappropriation.

clue.text: Saying "When" ought to show what you've had

indicators.note: the letters show themselves, already visible inside the words beside them

blocks.note: surface padding: introduces the quoted word
running across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone pouring a drink is told to stop by a guest who has had plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying 'When' is how a guest tells the pourer to stop, so the surface hints at the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Having had enough is the idiom for having reached one's limit; the answer completes 'you've had ___'.

clue.text: 1 23 and 26 are enemies: plot incompetently at separating them?

indicators.note: work done incompetently is botched, so these letters come out in a muddle
to separate a word is to push something into its middle

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
an archaic word for enemies

explanation.surface: Rival railwaymen bungle a scheme to keep each other apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the answers ENGINE DRIVER and STOKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Footplatemen are the crew of a steam locomotive, the driver and fireman who stand on its platform.

clue.text: Contracts among sets that may be false

blocks.note: among means in
sets of false teeth

explanation.surface: Agreements hidden among papers might be forgeries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sets' suggests groups; here they are sets of teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Indentures are formal legal agreements, especially those binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Put down one's nose?

definitions.note: the answer describes a type of nose

blocks.note: first meaning: to rebuff or slight someone
second meaning: a short, turned-up kind of nose

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as lowering your nose; the snooty gesture of turning up your nose fits the slight too.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub is to ignore pointedly, and a snub nose is short and upturned.

clue.text: See 22
Cubist, second half first, with companion round hardwood tree

indicators.note: the back half of the name is brought round to the front

blocks.note: Georges Braque, co-founder of Cubism with Picasso
Companion of Honour, a British order
a round letter

explanation.surface: A Cubist painter, swapped about, goes round a hardwood tree with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Georges Braque founded Cubism with Picasso; the Companion of Honour is a British order, abbreviated CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Quebracho is a South American tree with extremely hard timber, its name meaning axe-breaker in Spanish.

clue.text: Guns, if raised, back original work

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word lifts its last letter to the top, so it reads upwards

blocks.note: the word if, read upwards
the rear is the back
a manuscript is the original of a written work

explanation.surface: Guns, if lifted up, would support an artist's creation.
explanation.definitionFit: Firearms are portable weapons such as rifles and pistols, which is what guns means.

clue.text: Vegetable cooked by a cleric without energy

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so these words go around the next piece
cooked food has been transformed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A vegetable dish is prepared by a tired priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like it means minus, but here it means outside, so E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Celeriac is a variety of celery grown for its swollen edible root, a vegetable.

clue.text: The oriental heaven is a form of cold storage

blocks.note: E for east
the sky is the heavens

explanation.surface: An Eastern paradise is said to be a kind of refrigeration.
explanation.walkthrough: An Esky is the Australian brand name for a portable cool box.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia an Esky is the everyday term for an insulated picnic cooler for keeping drinks chilled.

clue.text: Tommy's flowers have lost their tops

definitions.note: the answer is Tommy's surname, not a possessive

indicators.note: losing a top removes the first letter, in a down entry the uppermost one

blocks.note: catkins are the dangling flower clusters of willow and hazel

explanation.surface: A soldier's bouquet has been decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Atkins is the traditional name for a British private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy Atkins is the stock name for an ordinary British soldier, so Atkins is Tommy's surname.

clue.text: Principal expression at Roundhill getsgoing

blocks.note: the star is the leading performer
a term is a word or expression
read as round (O, a round letter) and hill (TOR, a rocky hill as on Dartmoor)

explanation.surface: The headmaster's speech at a school called Roundhill gets things under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundhill' is printed as one word, but splits into round and hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter motor is the electric motor that cranks a car engine so that it starts running.

clue.text: Dog going right across?

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
to go across is to go over

explanation.surface: A dog crosses to the right-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover is the stock name for a dog, and a rover also goes across country.
explanation.definitionFit: Rover is a traditional pet name for a dog, standing for any canine.

clue.text: Jo is Queen, as I wanted, having that mysterious quality

indicators.note: the letters are wanted in another form, a call to remake them

blocks.note: every letter of these words

explanation.surface: A girl called Jo is crowned queen, just as the speaker hoped, and she has a certain charm.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means literally 'I don't know what'.
explanation.definitionFit: The borrowed French expression names an indefinable attractive quality that cannot be described.

clue.text: See 1
Changed over, on, or off

blocks.note: surface reading: a list of ways something might be altered
setter's reading: a word that pairs with over, on and off to describe toggling and swapping

explanation.walkthrough: The answer combines with each of over, on and off to give a phrase, and on its own means changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping something or flicking a light are both actions of changing state, which the past-tense verb covers.

clue.text: A quick coffee?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cup gulped down in a hurry
setter's reading: the name of the drink comes from the Italian for pressed out, but recalls express, fast

explanation.walkthrough: The drink is often taken to mean express coffee, made swiftly under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: This strong Italian coffee is brewed in seconds by forcing steam through grounds and drunk quickly.

clue.text: Fireman associated with vampires

blocks.note: first meaning: the person who feeds a steam engine's furnace
second meaning: Bram ..., author of Dracula

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fireman' suggests a firefighter, but it is the old railway job of tending the boiler.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal-shovelling locomotive crewman tends the fire, and the Irish novelist wrote the famous Count Dracula tale.
